notes: Tranche 3 of the atomization migration: the decomposable 3-sentence prescriptions, run post-swap (lane: prescriptive skips descriptive-lane completeness; only named entries are touched). Same dispositions as spec.json. The rest of the 3-sentence tier stays as-is: enum registries and schema contracts are already in target shape, discrete action-items carry their work description, and norm-plus-elaboration claims are keeps per the b402 rewrite/decompose boundary.

cb:b118.claim: Every primitive sourced from a document or email carries an evidence array with source details including dates and specific descriptions of what was observed: the claim is the agent's interpretation, the evidence carries the factual basis.
atoms: The gap between claim and evidence is where misinterpretation lives and can be audited.

cb:b424.claim: Behavioral invariants belong in DAG contracts, not scattered across the agent-instruction file, struct definitions, or skill prose.
invariants: Every code module encoding domain rules has a corresponding DAG contract
Agent-instruction files (a skill definition, the agent-instruction file) translate intent and reference the DAG; they do not carry logic of their own

cb:b428.claim: User-sourced and manually-sourced provenance is authoritative.
invariants: Sync passes that would overwrite a user-sourced field with a different derived value surface the conflict instead of silently overwriting
Authorization to sync does not include authorization to discard user judgment

cb:b436.claim: Removal or renaming of a field from the assertion schema happens via DAG-authorized schema migration; individual node fields remain immutable outside authorized migrations.
invariants: A migration carries a compound belief asserting the decision, with deps citing this meta-convention and the primitive(s) carrying the new schema rules - the compound is the audit anchor and the citation point for future references, the primitives carry the schema content
A migration is adjudicated through the consensus mechanism (once built) or direct user authorization (interim)
The bulk transformation executes under the compound's authority
Any contract the migration conflicts with is superseded or retired
b029's per-node immutability permits this class of operation and no other

cb:b441.claim: Sub-agent delegation is permissible specifically for adjudication tasks - reviewing a session's proposed beliefs against the current graph, producing merge/reject decisions with reasons - and the carve-out does not extend to other classes of work (research, refactoring, design, plan execution) without an explicit new belief justifying it.
atoms: Adjudication has bounded input, bounded output, and the working-out is itself the artifact, so no understanding is hidden from the user.

cb:b465.claim: Contracts are never compiled into code: the contract-to-code relationship is verification, not generation - interpreters query a contract and the test suite asserts the code conforms (the `verify_against_contract` pattern, cb:b417 / cb:b425), so drift surfaces as a failing test, not a regenerated module.
atoms: Spec-to-code generation is nondeterministic and unmaintainable.

cb:b475.claim: Primitive atomicity doctrine: a primitive is one atomic statement of what a single source said, leaning verbatim - a primitive whose claim conjoins separable assertions is a mis-authored compound and is split at authoring time.
invariants: Atomicity is judgment, enforced in the write flow rather than by a verifier check; source-checkable verbatim predicates are future work for cached sources

cb:b525.claim: The repository README is a succinct front door - pitch, the two commitments, use cases, the sixty-second demo, quick start, a documentation map, honest status - and stays near 100 lines.
invariants: Narrative, reference, and worked-example material lives in docs/ files linked from the README's Documentation section (mental-model.md, codepaths.md, eval-ledger.md, reference.md, worked-example-eval-verdict.md)
New deep material is added as or into a docs/ file and linked from the map, never appended to the README
